sentence: This project builds an automated pipeline that uses machine learning to find and measure features in solar images.
This project studies how to design cryptosystems that resist attacks from future quantum computers.
This project develops machine-learning methods that make clear images from limited or corrupted measurements using little training data.
This project builds modular robotic swimmers that evolve through rounds of testing and learn to swim well in challenging flow conditions.
This project studies how male abdomen pigmentation arose and changed in fruit fly species by comparing the genes involved.
This project studies how electric pulsing can heal cracks and pores in nickel-based alloys made by additive manufacturing.
This project builds semiconductor lasers from magnesium zinc oxide that give off deep ultraviolet light.
This project builds hands-on exercises that show how code suggested by AI-powered coding assistant tools can be insecure and exploited.
This project studies how urban development and climate change affect hurricane wind risks to a building exterior using wind tunnel tests.
This project tests whether electromagnetic waves can detect brain activity in a non-invasive way, using changes in the dielectric properties of brain tissue.
This project builds computer models that automatically analyze the grammar of very large collections of historical text.
This project studies whether using generative AI to write, critique, and refine practice problems improves problem-solving skills in a physics course.
This project uses DNA and physical features of ironweed plants in the Eastern Hemisphere to sort their species into the correct genera.
This project builds deep learning tools that simulate cardiovascular fluid-structure interaction and measure how uncertain the results are.
This project studies how ruthenium compounds containing oligothiophene behave in their excited states and in redox reactions.
This project studies how invasive faucet snails and their trematode parasites spread and adapt to new habitats, using genomic sequencing and infection experiments.
This project designs robotic grippers that switch between a few stiffness states to handle live seafood safely.
